name: Ageratina

project_scope.scope_note: Both source-pool Ageratina species are canonical learner records; their native-range metadata remains unchanged.

study_strategy.warning: Many fall composites need comparison by structure, not just bloom color.

fast_fill_note: Canonical PASS Ageratina altissima now has a 3-image learner gallery covering whole-plant habit, white discoid heads, and an additional exact-species field reference.
look_here_first: Check stem base and persistent leaves: white mistflower / shrubby boneset (A. havanensis) is an evergreen or nearly evergreen shrub with woody, brittle stems, while white snakeroot (A. altissima) is an herbaceous perennial. For definitive fruiting separation, FNA describes A. havanensis CYPSELAE as hairy (hispid), and A. altissima as glabrous; inspect a mature fruit under magnification.
shared_genus_traits: Terminal clusters of many small capitula containing disk florets without ray florets
Phyllaries form an involucre around each head; mature cypselae bear a bristly pappus

species_comparison_matrix.ageratina_altissima: Erect, herbaceous perennial (fibrous crown, sometimes rhizomatous); leaves not persistent on woody shrub framework
species_comparison_matrix.ageratina_havanensis: Evergreen or persistent-leaved shrub/subshrub with brittle woody stems; FNA notes unique evergreen leaves among U.S. Ageratina

species_comparison_matrix.priority: PRIMARY fruiting-stage reproductive separator; high-magnification matched photos needed

species_comparison_matrix.ageratina_altissima: Commonly 4–11 × 2.5–8 cm, broadly deltate-ovate/ovate, coarsely doubly incised-serrate
species_comparison_matrix.ageratina_havanensis: Commonly 3–5 × 2–5 cm, deltate to ovate/hastate, toothed

species_comparison_matrix.priority: Overlapping; DO NOT use as decisive separator

species_comparison_matrix.ageratina_altissima: Shadier woodland-edge or disturbed patches, often erect to 120 cm
species_comparison_matrix.ageratina_havanensis: Limestone bluffs/ledges, slopes, oak-juniper; shrub 30–200 cm
Small white to faintly pinkish discoid capitula

quick_comparison_steps: 1. Confirm opposite toothed leaves and clusters of many small rayless heads (one head = many tiny florets).
2. Inspect old basal stems and leaf persistence: brittle woody framework/persistent foliage suggests A. havanensis; herbaceous perennial crown suggests A. altissima.
3. Compare mature leaf blades plus petioles: A. havanensis typically shorter petioles/smaller leaves, but overlap requires caution.
4. At maturity photograph several CYPSELAE with scale; FNA: hairy = A. havanensis, glabrous = A. altissima.
5. Photograph head side/phyllary series to distinguish these from Chromolaena odorata and Eupatorium serotinum.
overlap_and_cautions: Both species can have opposite toothed triangular leaves and white rayless flower heads; flower color alone cannot separate them.
Leaf size, branching density and flatness of head clusters vary with growth conditions and are only supporting cues.
Basal woodiness may be hard to assess on a young shoot; examine the plant base or previous-season branches.
A. havanensis native-range certification is not resolved by this comparison; preserve its existing learner/range status.
A. altissima contains toxic compounds; do not taste plants as an identification method.

external_mistflower_comparison.look_here_first: Long cylindrical individual heads with 8–10 mm involucre in 4–6+ series; usually larger, often sprawling subshrub. Do not use bloom color.
Rhizomatous perennial with shorter, hemispheric heads, blue-violet disk florets, triangular toothed undissected leaves
Dissected lobed leaves with shorter, hemispheric heads; floral color overlaps other mistflowers
Tall leafy herb with white heads; photograph branching, leaf attachment and individual involucres before relying on habit

authoritative_morphology_notes: FNA A. havanensis: evergreen-persistent opposite leaves, petioles 3–10(–15) mm, blades about 3–5 cm, involucres 4–6 mm, stems shrubs (often 69–150 cm) on limestone slopes; leaves eglandular.
For A. altissima use mature opposite coarsely dentate petiolate leaves and rhizomatous non-woody base; size/head color alone is insufficient.
Chromolaena odorata can share an upright shrubby form and white-pinkish heads, but its involucres are noticeably elongated/cylindrical (8–10 mm) and phyllaries have more series.
